memo:
### Position read
Opening position. We moved Red from (0,3) to (3,3), claiming the upper-left center square; losses remain 0 for every color.

### Our plan
Contest the center with both colors while preserving rook lanes. If the opponent occupies a central square, seek same-color sandwiches or enclosure rather than blindly filling around it. Yellow can approach from below, especially through columns 3–4.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.

### Lessons
Only the moving color can form sandwich flanks; teammate pieces do not help and may be captured as part of a mixed line or group. Moving into a sandwich is safe until an opponent move triggers capture.

### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. The opponent has Blue at (3,4). Losses remain 0. Green acts next.

### Our plan
Red has a direct sandwich capture: move the Red piece at (0,5) to (3,5), capturing Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). Green appears unable to block (3,5) or remove the Red flank immediately. Afterward, reinforce the center with additional pieces rather than vacating existing central occupants.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent answered our first center claim by placing Blue adjacent at (3,4), overlooking or accepting the same-color Red sandwich threat.

### Lessons
Before each move, scan for a landing square on the far side of an adjacent line; only matching-color endpoints count. Maintain open files from the starting edges to tactical landing squares.

### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; the opponent occupies (4,3) with Green. This move captures Blue at (3,4), giving Blue 1 loss. Red also stands at (3,5). Blue acts next.

### Our plan
Preserve our two central occupants and contest (4,3). Seek a Yellow sandwich against Green using Yellow endpoints, or maneuver Yellow toward (3,4) while ensuring the opponent cannot claim all four centers. Red’s pieces at (3,3) and (3,5) may create further horizontal traps.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent challenges central control directly, first with Blue at (3,4), then Green at (4,3). Blue’s placement allowed an immediate Red sandwich capture.

### Lessons
Central occupation can create tactical liabilities: scan every line through each center piece for same-color flanks. Void status is irrelevant so far; losses are Red 0, Blue 1, Yellow 0, Green 0.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; Green occupies (4,3), while (3,4) is empty. Blue has 1 loss. Yellow has advanced to (4,1), with (4,2) empty between it and Green.

### Our plan
Threaten Yellow (4,1)->(4,2), sandwiching Green at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4). If Green vacates the center, consider bringing Yellow from (7,3) to (4,3). Preserve our central pieces and work toward occupying (3,4) without vacating (4,4) prematurely.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly but moved Blue from (5,7) to (5,2) after losing the Blue center piece. Expect Green to respond immediately to the sandwich threat.

### Lessons
Same-color endpoints are decisive: the Yellow at (4,4) makes lateral pressure on Green possible. Recheck whether any defense merely relocates Green into another Yellow sandwich.

### Position read
We now hold (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. Green holds (4,3) and also has a piece at (2,3); Red at (3,3) is visually between them but is safe because captures trigger only from the mover's landing square. Blue has 1 loss; we have 1 Red loss.

### Our plan
Aim to add Red at (3,4), likely via (0,4), while preserving both current center pieces. Yellow still threatens (4,1)->(4,2), capturing Green at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4), unless Blue blocks (4,2). If Blue plays (5,2)->(4,2), reassess the mixed Blue-Green line and develop another Yellow toward the center rather than abandoning (4,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center tactically and previously used Green (2,0)->(2,3) to capture our former Red center piece. Blue’s most direct defense now is occupying (4,2).

### Lessons
A piece moving into an apparent enemy sandwich remains safe. Central occupation is immediate victory, so secure center squares can outweigh speculative edge captures.

### Position read
We hold Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,4). The opponent blocks the lower-left center with Green (4,3) and Blue (4,2); Blue has 1 loss and we have 1 Red loss. Yellow is now staged safely at (6,3), while Green also has (2,3).

### Our plan
Preserve both center anchors. Red should occupy (3,4) from (0,4) if still legal and tactically safe. Yellow at (6,3) is a reserve for (4,3) whenever Green vacates and (5,3) remains clear. The horizontal mixed Blue-Green line can be captured only after a Yellow move lands at (4,1) or (4,4) with uninterrupted Yellow flanks, so track any chance to force Green away.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests center tactically: Green previously captured a Red center piece from (2,3), and Blue answered our pressure by moving to (4,2). Expect Green to obstruct the third file or prepare sandwiches against advancing Yellow.

### Lessons
Do not place Yellow on (5,3) while Green remains at (4,3): Green can land at (6,3) and sandwich it. Preserve established center occupation unless moving an anchor creates a concrete capture.

### Position read
We now occupy three center squares: Red at (3,3) and (3,4), Yellow at (4,4); (4,3) is empty. Yellow at (6,3) cannot reach it while Green remains at (5,3). Blue at (4,2) can enter (4,3). Losses: our Red 1, opponent Blue 1.

### Our plan
Preserve the three center anchors and find a way to clear or bypass Green (5,3). If (5,3) becomes empty while (4,3) stays empty, Yellow (6,3) can land on (4,3), sandwich Blue (4,2) against Yellow (4,1), and complete center occupation. Avoid moving Red into (4,3): Blue (4,7) could then land at (4,5) and sandwich both it and Yellow (4,4) against Blue (4,2).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively blocks center routes and may now place Blue (4,2) onto (4,3), or reposition Green while maintaining control of file 3.

### Lessons
Check long mixed-color sandwiches before filling gaps. Our separate Red center pair is currently safe because empty (4,3) breaks Blue’s row-4 sandwich line.

### Position read
Yellow moved (7,2)->(4,2), sandwiching Blue (4,3) against Yellow (4,4). Blue now has 2 losses. We hold Red (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow (4,2),(4,4), with center (4,3) empty immediately after capture. Green (5,3) can answer by moving to (4,3); because Green (2,3) is the far flank, that move would capture Red (3,3) and raise Red to 2 losses.

### Our plan
If Green does not occupy (4,3) or otherwise break the center, preserve both Red anchors and aim to move Yellow (4,2)->(4,3) for center victory. If Green enters (4,3), use the spare Yellow at (4,1): first clear Yellow (4,2), then later land (4,1)->(4,2) to sandwich Green against Yellow (4,4), if the formation survives. Seek one more Blue capture to eliminate Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent blocks immediate center wins and uses safe entry into apparent sandwiches. Green’s file-3 formation creates a direct tactical capture on Red (3,3).

### Lessons
Use the bottom Yellow rather than the (4,1) piece so the latter remains a reusable flanker. Captured pieces leave empty squares; sandwiching the center blocker does not itself complete center occupation.

### Position read
We have Red at (3,2),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,1),(4,2),(4,4). Green occupies (4,3), with another Green at (2,3). Losses: we have Red 2, Yellow 0; opponent has Blue 2, Green 0. The center is split: (3,3) empty, (3,4) ours, (4,3) opponent, (4,4) ours.

### Our plan
Red (3,2) can later move to (3,3), completing our top-center pair while preserving (3,4). Yellow must dislodge Green from (4,3): move one current horizontal flanker away and return it to trigger the stale sandwich, then occupy the vacated center square on a later Yellow turn. Prefer any safe opportunity to capture one more Blue and eliminate that color.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent consistently blocks immediate center wins and exploits same-color flank geometry. Expect Green to contest (3,3), move the (4,3) blocker, or disrupt Yellow’s row-4 sandwich formation.

### Lessons
Existing sandwiches do not capture until a normal piece of the flanking color lands and triggers them. After a center blocker is captured, its square is empty and still must be occupied to win.

### Position read
We have Red at (3,2),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,1),(4,4), with the moved Yellow now at (5,2). Green remains at center (4,3), and another Green is at (2,3). Losses: Red 2, Yellow 0; Blue 2, Green 0. Center: (3,3) empty, (3,4) ours, (4,3) opponent, (4,4) ours.

### Our plan
The Yellow move vacated (4,2), preparing a return there to trigger the sandwich against Green at (4,3). If that Green moves left to (4,2), Yellow can instead land at (4,3) from (4,4), sandwiching it against Yellow at (4,1) and occupying center. If Green leaves row 4 elsewhere, prioritize occupying (4,3). Red still aims to occupy (3,3) when safe. Capture one more Blue whenever available to eliminate it.

### Opponent tendencies
Expect Green to use (3,3) as its strongest escape from (4,3), simultaneously blocking our remaining empty center. The opponent consistently contests immediate center completion.

### Lessons
A moved piece entering an existing sandwich is safe; capture requires a later landing by the flanking color. Preserve alternate flank geometry so an escaping blocker can still be punished.

### Position read
Red moved from (3,2) to (2,2), preserving Red at (3,4). Green occupies both remaining contested center squares, (3,3) and (4,3). Yellow at (5,2) can land (4,2) and sandwich Green (4,3) against Yellow (4,4). Losses remain Red 2, Yellow 0; Blue 2, Green 0.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, prioritize (5,2)->(4,2) if still legal, capturing Green at (4,3). If Green at (3,3) stays through its turn, Red can return (2,2)->(3,2), sandwiching it against Red (3,4). If it leaves, seek to occupy (3,3) without vacating (3,4), ideally using Red from (2,3)/(3,2) geometry. After clearing the lower blocker, move Yellow into (4,3) while retaining (4,4). Capture one more Blue whenever available to eliminate it.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green to contest central completion and may shift the upper Green into (4,3) after the lower one is captured. Blue may try to interfere with Yellow’s prepared landing or attack vulnerable Red, whose next loss eliminates it.

### Lessons
Do not place Red at (3,1): Green could land at (3,2) and sandwich it against Green at (3,0), causing Red’s third loss. Vertical flank resets are safer.

### Position read
Yellow moved (7,5)->(6,5), sandwiching Blue at (6,4) against Yellow at (6,3). This is Blue’s third loss, so Blue is eliminated and its remaining pieces at (1,7), (2,4), and (4,7) become Void. Green still holds (3,3) and (4,3); we hold (3,4) and (4,4). Our losses: Red 2, Yellow 0. Green has 0 losses.

### Our plan
Clear both Green center blockers. If Green at (3,3) remains, Red can use (2,2)->(3,2) to sandwich it against Red at (3,4). Yellow still has (5,2)->(4,2) available to sandwich Green at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4), unless Green disrupts it. Then occupy the vacated center squares while preserving (3,4) and (4,4). Protect Red carefully because one more Red loss eliminates it.

### Opponent tendencies
Green must now defend both contested center squares and may move one blocker or attack Red’s fragile formation. Eliminated Blue can still move Void pieces to block routes or contest center, but cannot capture.

### Lessons
Always check newly moved pieces for an immediate third-loss sandwich; eliminating a color removes its capture threat even though its Void pieces remain active blockers.

### Position read
Red moved (0,1)->(3,1), sandwiching Green at (3,2) and (3,3) against Red at (3,4). Green now has 2 losses and only (4,3) remains in the center. Blue is eliminated; its Void pieces cannot capture. Our center pieces remain at (3,4) and (4,4). Red has 2 losses, so it remains fragile.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s next turn, play (5,2)->(4,2) to sandwich Green at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4). This should inflict Green’s third loss and eliminate it; Blue’s current Void pieces cannot reach or block (4,2). Afterward, occupy the cleared central squares (3,3) and (4,3) while preserving our existing two center pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent tried to reinforce the row-3 center, but placed two Green pieces in one capturable line. Void Blue can reposition as a blocker but poses no capture threat.

### Lessons
When an opponent extends a center chain, check whether a same-color far anchor turns the entire chain into a sandwich.

### Position read
Yellow’s move (5,2)->(4,2) sandwiches Green at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4). This gives Green its third loss. Since Blue is already eliminated, the opponent’s two colors are now eliminated.

### Our plan
The winning move has been played; the game should end immediately by team elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s center reinforcement formed capturable straight lines against our same-color anchors.

### Lessons
Before pursuing center occupation, always check for an immediate team-elimination capture; a single sandwich can decide the game.
